title: Sóng 2 — UX cảm nhận được ngay (M3-A3 wheel acceleration, M3-A7 keyed notice queue, M3-D3 transcript scroll chrome)
wave: 2 (plan lines 7294-7346; the whole wave is exactly these three items — A3, A7, D3)
one_line: Fast-scrolling a mouse wheel now speeds up the way a trackpad always has, transient status lines get keys so a newer one can replace an older one instead of scrolling away forever, and the agent transcript overlay grows an unread divider you can click to jump back.
user_visible_effect: Wheel scrolling feels the same on a clicky wheel and a trackpad instead of being hard-coded to three rows per notch, with a `ui.mouseWheelSpeedMultiplier` setting to slow it down or speed it up. Status messages that mean 'the same thing' (compaction counts, background-job progress) replace each other on one line above the prompt instead of accumulating as permanent transcript lines. In the agent transcript viewer, a rule and an unread-count pill appear at the first message you have not read; activating it jumps back to the newest message.

steps.instruction: A3 STEP 0 — DO THIS BEFORE ANY CODE. Run the measurement table on four real terminals (Ghostty, Terminal.app, VS Code, Cursor). For each, record: (a) how many SGR wheel reports one physical detent produces, (b) the inter-report gap for a trackpad continuous scroll, (c) whether a detent emits a direction flip-then-flip-back and how long the pair spans, (d) the gap after which the terminal stops sending. Write the three resulting numbers into the work item as `WHEEL_BATCH_WINDOW_MS`, `WHEEL_BOUNCE_WINDOW_MS`, `WHEEL_IDLE_RESET_MS`, plus the ramp cap. The plan's 200/1500/5 are placeholders, not a spec. Do not write a line of TypeScript before this table exists — the model cannot be tuned and the tests cannot be pinned without it.

A3 STEP 1 — create the module. Pure `resolveWheelDelta(notches, thresholds)` that turns a synthesized notch stream into `{ rows, source }`; a `WheelThresholds` record (batchWindowMs, bounceWindowMs, idleResetMs, maxRowsPerNotch) so the measured values live in one exported constant; a thin per-pane `WheelAccelerationState` with `reset()` that owns the notch history and hands it to the pure function; and `setWheelSpeedMultiplier` / `wheelSpeedMultiplier` for the user override, applied exactly once, after the model. Keep it a function plus a thin state shell — the plan's biggest risk is that a ramp that lags feels worse than a wrong constant.

A3 STEP 2 — attach the clock. Add `now: number` to `SgrMouseEvent`; give `parseSgrMouse` and `routeSgrMouseInput` an optional trailing `now` parameter defaulting to `Date.now()`; widen `SelectListMouseTarget.handleWheel` to `(delta: number, now?: number)`; and have `routeSelectListMouse` pass `event.now`. Keep `now` optional on `handleWheel` so a target that ignores it compiles — but see the open question, the recommendation is NOT to accelerate the list targets at all, in which case this widening is the whole change to them.

A3 STEP 3 — convert the eight constant sites, one at a time, and re-verify the count after each: agent-transcript-viewer.ts:470, plan-review-overlay.ts:580, rewind-selector.ts:245, copy-selector.ts:214, git-tui.ts:697, raw-sse.ts:168, log-viewer.ts:639 (all x3) and usage-dashboard.ts:759 (x2). At rewind-selector and copy-selector the repaint stays gated on the scroll actually moving — `transcript-browser.ts:175-180` `scroll()` returns false when the offset is unchanged, so pass a row count through, not a boolean.

A3 STEP 4 — the ninth site. Replace `delta * 3` in `handleWheel` with the model call and widen the signature at :896 to accept `now`. This is the one no `event.wheel * N` grep finds, and it is why git-tui's RIGHT pane is also x3 today — `:695` delegates to it. Add a `WheelAccelerationState` instance per pane: the sidebar gets its own, git-tui's main pane gets its own. Sharing one instance across panes is the plan's second-named risk: scrolling the sidebar would preload momentum for the other pane.

A3 STEP 5 — declare the escape hatch. Register `ui.mouseWheelSpeedMultiplier` (type number, default 1) with a `validate` that throws on 0, negatives, and non-finite values, and wire it with `effect(cfgUiMouseWheelSpeedMultiplier, setWheelSpeedMultiplier)` exactly as `cfgTuiMaxInlineImageColumns` does at :334-341. Before you write the `ui:` block, read the open question: a `UiNumber` with no `options` is deliberately hidden from the settings panel, so this setting as specified is config-file only.

A7 STEP 1 — name the options type and keep the signature compatible. Declare and export `ShowStatusOptions` (dim, immediate, invalidates, fold, key) and change the parameter type in place. All 332 existing `showStatus(...)` call lines must compile untouched — that is the whole point of naming the type rather than changing the shape. Branch inside the method: no `key` means today's `chatContainer` path byte-for-byte; a `key` means the keyed queue. Never merge the two branches.

A7 STEP 2 — build the keyed row's home. Add a dedicated `noticeContainer` beside the other layout containers and put it in the layout array immediately before `hookWidgetContainerAbove`. Do NOT reuse `hookWidgetContainerAbove`: `ExtensionUIController.#renderHookWidgetContainer` calls `container.clear()` at extension-ui-controller.ts:394 on every hook-widget rebuild, so a notice row placed there is silently wiped. Do NOT route the notice through the composer top chrome either — `syncComposerShape` at interactive-mode.ts:3054-3068 hands the editor a `TopBorderProvider` that returns a pre-rendered string from `StatusLineComponent.getTopBorder` / `getBandTopBorder` / `getStandaloneTopBorder`; there is no component row to drop into.

A7 STEP 3 — implement the four option semantics in the keyed branch. `key` defaults to the message so today's in-place-edit behavior survives; `invalidates` removes every queued notice whose effective key matches, compared against the TARGET's key, so to evict an unkeyed notice you must pass its exact message string; `fold` with the same key appends to the existing row instead of adding one; `immediate` bypasses the queue and applies its `invalidates` synchronously. Then make the compaction notice keyed with a stable key so repeated compactions replace each other instead of stacking.

A7 STEP 4 — route the notice event. `#handleNotice` keeps `showError` and `showWarning` exactly as they are (durable, must not be evicted) and gives the `info` branch a key so two notices of the same kind supersede. The `notice` event carries no key today, so the key is chosen here, not read off the event.

D3 STEP 1 — do NOT build a new anchoring mechanism; it already exists. `ChatTranscriptBuilder.rowForEntry(entryId)` (chat-transcript-builder.ts:138-144) maps an entry id to a logical row, `#frame` already turns that into a `ScrollRangeAnchor` at :597-608, and `ScrollView.revealRange` / `hasRevealedRange` / `logicalRowAt` (scroll-view.ts:292 / :284 / :243) already do anchor-by-message-index with re-anchoring. D3 is: track the first unread entry id, paint a fixed-height divider plus a count pill at `rowForEntry(firstUnreadEntryId)`, and add a key that reveals the newest entry. Height-delta re-anchoring needs no new code because `revealRange` already re-derives the viewport from the anchor on every render.

D3 STEP 2 — leave `#handleScroll` alone. The pager keys (g/G/j/k plus the `handleScrollKey` delegation) already exist and already own the offset; the new chrome is a render concern, not a navigation concern. Do not touch the two renderer invariants in docs/tui-core-renderer.md:107 and :174 — an overlay anchoring on a logical row does not probe terminal scrollback, but do not weaken the wording either.

A3 + D3 + A7 STEP 4 — write the tests. Three new files and two extensions, in the order the work lands: the wheel model (pure, no terminal), the mouse wiring (including the two mandatory repairs to the existing exact-equality assertions and the `baseEvent` literal), the notice queue (including the compaction integration test and the render-location contract), and the transcript scroll chrome. Then the transcript byte-identity assertion: the plain transcript must render identically with the chrome in place.

FINAL AUDIT (not a test — run once, by hand, and paste the output into the work item). `grep -rn 'wheel \* [0-9]' packages/tui/src --include='*.ts'` must return zero hits and `grep -rn 'delta \* 3' packages/tui/src --include='*.ts'` must return zero hits. Nine sites is the count that matters: the eight constants plus the one inside `handleWheel`. The plan is explicit that no `event.wheel * N` grep is a sufficient counter — today it returns 8 while the true x3 site count is 9.

test_contract:
Four contracts, one per test file, none redundant.

(1) `packages/tui/test/wheel-acceleration.test.ts` defends THE MODEL: given a synthesized notch stream and the thresholds recorded in the measurement table, the returned row count is exactly the specified one. Detented wheel -> three notches for one physical detent stay at 1 row each, never 3. Continuous at ~20 ms -> climbs to the cap; at 500 ms -> stays at 1. Flip-then-flip-back inside the measured bounce window -> wheel mode on; no event for the measured idle-reset window -> off. A stream with no flip never enables wheel mode. Notches closer than the measured batch window count once. `ui.mouseWheelSpeedMultiplier = 0.5` multiplies the accelerated delta exactly ONCE (a double application is invisible in the model test but doubles the speed for the user). If this regresses, the user feels a wrong scroll speed on their own hardware and there is no way for them to tell you — only the threshold table can.

(2) `packages/tui/test/mouse.test.ts` defends THE WIRING: `routeSelectListMouse` hands `event.now` to `handleWheel` as a second argument, and `parseSgrMouse` stamps a `now` derived from the injected clock rather than calling `Date.now()` internally (so the test can assert the exact value). The two pre-existing assertions — the `toEqual` at :22-32 and the `baseEvent` literal at :126-134 — are the canary: if a future change drops the field from one construction path, they go red.

(3) `packages/coding-agent/test/notice-queue.test.ts` defends TWO contracts and the second one is the one that matters. First: supersession and folding — a keyed low-priority notice followed by an `immediate` notice whose `invalidates` names its key removes the first from the display permanently; the same key posted three times with `fold` accumulates into exactly one row; a notice arriving while another is showing queues rather than overwrites. Second, and NON-NEGOTIABLE: THE RENDER-LOCATION CONTRACT — a keyed notice appears in the notice container's children and is ABSENT from `chatContainer.children`; an unkeyed notice is still in `chatContainer.children` exactly as before. Without that assertion the build stays green while someone renders both branches into the transcript, which is precisely the unrequested behavior change the plan forbids. Plus one integration test driving a real compaction through `EventController` and asserting exactly ONE transient notice results, and a validation test proving 0 and negatives are rejected rather than applied.

(4) `packages/tui/test/transcript-viewer-scroll-chrome.test.ts` defends THE MARKER: scroll up, append a message, the divider shows with the right unread count, activating it returns to the bottom; change terminal width through at least three widths WHILE scrolled and the marker still points at the same message; and the plain transcript renders byte-identically with the chrome in place. The width test is the whole reason this item exists — a chrome header whose height varies shifts the viewport on every reflow even when the offset is unchanged. If this regresses, the divider drifts onto the wrong message the first time the user resizes their window mid-scroll, and nothing else catches it.

gate_can_fail: Yes, and each clause fails for a distinct reason. (a) fails if the implementer copies the plan's placeholder numbers instead of measuring — the numbers are visible in the diff. (b) fails on any type error, including the SgrMouseEvent widening that touches 20+ routeMouse implementations. (c) fails if a test file is missing, empty, or its assertions are vacuous. (d) is the specific clause that catches the failure mode the plan warns about: a build where someone renders both the keyed and unkeyed branches into the transcript stays perfectly green without it. (e) is the clause that catches an unrequested behavior change to 332 existing call sites — the pre-existing assertions are the tripwire. (f) fails if a site was missed, and it is the only check that catches the ninth site, since no `event.wheel * N` grep reaches `delta * 3` inside `handleWheel`. (g) cannot be automated at all, which is why it is a gate rather than a step.

Any later wave item that adds its own scroll surface must route through `packages/tui/src/mouse-wheel.ts` instead of introducing a second multiplier — that is the AGENTS.md 'two implementations of the same thing is a bug' rule applied to scroll speed.
effort: The plan budgets L/~5 days for A3, M/~3 for A7, M/~2 for D3 — about 10 days for the wave. My estimate after verification is closer to 6-7, and the difference is entirely in D3 and in the A3 measurement: D3's hardest part (anchor by message index, survive reflow) is ALREADY IMPLEMENTED (`ChatTranscriptBuilder.rowForEntry` -> `ScrollRangeAnchor` -> `ScrollView.revealRange`), so D3 is a render-and-keybinding job, roughly S/1 day, not M/2. A3's 5 days are real but only ~1.5 of them are code: the measurement table is irreducible calendar time and the plan is right that it should not be split across two people. A7 is 3 days and I would hold it at 2.5-3: the code is small, but proving the composer row and the transcript row never mix is the entire budget, exactly as the plan says. The wave's real risk is not effort, it is that A3's measurement never happens and placeholder numbers ship.
risk: The single most likely way to get this wrong is to accept the plan's framing that the six `handleWheel` implementations are 'accelerated' alongside the nine scroll sites. They are not the same thing, and I verified every one of them: `SelectList.handleWheel` calls `this.#selection.move(delta)` (select-list.ts:229-231), `SettingsList.handleWheel` calls `this.#moveSelection(delta, false)` (settings-list.ts:241-247), `AgentHub.handleWheel` does `this.#selectedActivityRow + delta` (agent-hub.ts:1254), `SessionSelector` and `OAuthSelector` call `this.#menu.move(delta, false)`, and `ExtensionList` calls `#moveSelectionUp()` / `#moveSelectionDown()` (extension-list.ts:597-600). Those are SELECTION moves of exactly one row, not scrolls. Multiplying them by 3 makes a wheel notch silently skip two rows the user never saw pass, in a list where the pointer may be highlighting the row they are about to click. The plan never defines an acceleration semantic for them, and its own risk section is entirely about scroll lag. Worse, the plan's list of forwarding call sites is incomplete — beyond `routeSelectListMouse` there are five more that would silently keep the old behavior: oauth-selector.ts:422, session-selector.ts:1134, settings-selector.ts:689 (which reaches `handleWheel` through `handleWheelAt` at settings-list.ts:249-255), extension-dashboard.ts:282, and git-tui.ts:695. The recommendation is to accelerate ONLY the nine scroll sites, leave the six selection movers at exactly one row, and answer open question 1 before anyone writes the interface change.
open_questions: OPEN QUESTION 1 — BLOCKING. What does 'acceleration' mean for the six `handleWheel(delta: -1 | 1)` implementations, given that every one of them is a one-row SELECTION move rather than a scroll (verified: select-list.ts:229, settings-list.ts:241, agent-hub.ts:1247, session-selector.ts:588, oauth-selector.ts:407, extension-list.ts:597)? Recommendation: do NOT accelerate them. Keep one notch = one row for selection, and apply the model only to the nine scroll sites. If the product owner does want list acceleration, it needs its own, much lower cap and its own decision — and the five extra forwarding call sites must be updated too, or the behavior is inconsistent between overlays.

OPEN QUESTION 2 — BLOCKING for the setting's shape. `ui.mouseWheelSpeedMultiplier` as specified is `type: "number"` with no `ui.options`, and `registry.ts:42-43` says a numeric setting without options is DELIBERATELY HIDDEN from the settings panel. So as specified it is config-file only. Is that acceptable for an 'escape hatch', or does it need a submenu of discrete values so users can actually reach it? If it stays config-file-only, say so in the changelog entry, because a user reading 'there is a setting' will look for it in the panel and not find it.

OPEN QUESTION 3 — non-blocking but decide now. Should the acceleration cap be a rows-per-notch integer or a float? Every current consumer truncates (`scroll-view.ts:352` does `Math.trunc(delta)`), so a float cap is silently floored per call and a ramp that grows 1→2→3 never lands mid-step. Integer is the safer default; confirm before the model is written.

OPEN QUESTION 4 — carried forward from the plan, explicitly NOT blocking. Whether a keyed transient status that has scrolled out of view should also be recorded in the transcript permanently, or whether the transcript is the complete record and notices are additive only. The plan leaves this open and correctly notes it does not block Wave 2 — A7 only has to keep the unkeyed branch's existing transcript behavior.

Re-anchoring across reflow needs no new code because `revealRange` re-derives the viewport from the anchor on every render. This drops D3 from M/2 days to roughly S/1 day, and the width test becomes a regression guard on existing machinery rather than the item's whole risk.
